account: Today I went to the mill for the scheduled ten o'clock grain inspection, but did not locate the miller. Neighbour said they had not seen the miller either. Several townsfolk have been repeating vague talk of a 'bridge or port change at bakery,' without clear details. I have not witnessed any such change, so I do not regard the reports as confirmed. Neighbour told me they saw Builder give Baker a lantern and planks last night, but did not know what they were for. I asked Baker directly; I heard no answer before leaving for lunch. Baker was busy baking, carrying wheat, and Builder was also at the bakery. The materials might be for lighting or building work there, but I cannot establish their purpose or any connection to the rumours. Separately, Builder arranged a great-hall lighting inspection with me for eighteen hundred today, and I asked Secretary to record it. I am now home, slightly late for noon lunch; council letters at the office are scheduled for thirteen hundred and tea with Neighbour for fifteen hundred.
